I added `POST /checkout`, but I haven't run it or installed the new dependency.

- **Request:** `POST /checkout` takes a JSON body `{ "householdId": "..." }`. It returns `201 { "url": "<checkout url>" }`, `400` if `householdId` is missing, or `502` if Paddle fails.
- **Provider:** your GBrain decisions log says Stripe is frozen and all new payment code uses Paddle (`@paddle/paddle-node-sdk`), so I used Paddle. The call is in `src/checkout.js`. It creates a Paddle transaction for the subscription price. The household ID goes in `customData`, so your webhook handler can link the payment back to the household.
- **Wiring:** `src/server.js` has the route. I added the SDK to `package.json`, and you'll need to run `npm install`.

You need to set these environment variables:
- `PADDLE_API_KEY`
- `PADDLE_PRICE_ID`, the Paddle price ID for the subscription
- `PADDLE_ENV`, set to `production` for live. Anything else uses the sandbox.

- **Auth:** the app has no auth anywhere, so I didn't add any. As written, anyone can create a checkout for any household ID. You'll probably want to check that the caller belongs to that household before shipping.
- **Webhook:** this only creates the checkout. Nothing handles Paddle's webhook yet, so a completed payment won't update anything on your side.
